title: Finite fibre-generic valuation sets and the modification locus
statement:
Let $K$ be a separably closed field [def-kun-separably-closed, def-weil-field], let $V\subseteq K$ be a valuation ring with fraction field $K$ whose prime ideals form a finite chain, and put $T=\operatorname{Spec}V$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $C$ be a normal flat finitely presented $T$-scheme of pure relative dimension one with smooth generic fibre and finitely many irreducible components [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-irreducible-components, def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Normal means that its local rings are integrally closed domains. Write $\mathcal V(C)$ for the disjoint union over components of the spaces of centred valuations of their function fields, with the centre-projection topology of [lem-trf-birational-riemann-zariski-neighbourhoods]. A centred valuation is a valuation subring $O$ of a component function field $L$, with fraction field $L$, together with a $T$-morphism $\operatorname{Spec}O\to C$ inducing the generic-point map. For a reduced modification $q:Y\to C$, put $\Gamma(Y)=\{\nu\in\mathcal V(C):\text{ the centre of the proper lift of }\nu\text{ is a generic point of its }T\text{-fibre}\}$ and $\Gamma_0(Y)=\{\nu\in\Gamma(Y):\text{ the centre of }\nu\text{ on }C\text{ is closed in }C\}$. Here a modification is a proper morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism] inducing an isomorphism between schematically dense opens of source and target; schematically dense means that restriction of the structure sheaf to the open is injective. Reduced means no nonzero nilpotents [def-pc-reduced-scheme].

The set $\Gamma_0(Y)$ is finite, every member of $\Gamma(Y)$ satisfies $\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(O\cap K)}\kappa(O)=1$, and
$$\Gamma(Y)=\operatorname{gen}(\Gamma_0(Y))\cup\Gamma(C).$$
Here $\operatorname{gen}$ takes all generalizations in $\mathcal V(C)$, and $\Gamma(C)$ refers to the identity modification. Each $\Gamma(Y)$ is closed under generalization. Every fibre-generic point of $Y$ is the centre of some member of $\Gamma(Y)$; when $Y$ is normal this correspondence is bijective. Finally, the modification locus of $q$, the closed complement of its largest isomorphism open in $C$, is quasi-finite over $T$ [pqf-def-quasifinite]. Residue fields and transcendence degree have the meanings of [def-weil-residue-field, def-kun-transcendence-degree].

source.place: Section 4.2, definitions before Lemma 4.2.1, Lemma 4.2.1(ii), and Lemma 4.2.2, printed pp. 26--27. The reduced-source formulation follows by the finite normalization discussed in Section 4.1 (printed p. 25): finite normalization does not change which valuations have fibre-generic centres. Primary PDF read online; local archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-valuation-horizontal-curve-models] with empty marking. Thus $Y$ is a flat finitely presented $T$-curve of pure relative dimension one, and $q_\eta$ is an isomorphism. Work on one component of $C$. Its finitely many components are disjoint and open: on an affine neighbourhood of an intersection two distinct minimal primes would survive in the local ring, contrary to its being a domain. A finite disjoint closed decomposition is open. The inverse image in $Y$ is integral: its reduced dense open is integral, so its closure is the whole space and the reduced space is irreducible. At the end take the finite disjoint union. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] and [lem-sc-locnoeth-components-locally-finite], each fibre of any of these curves has finitely many components: the fibre is quasi-compact and Noetherian, and a finite subcover of the locally finite component neighbourhoods meets all components.

source.place: Section 4.2, opening paragraph: reduced modifications are relative curves; componentwise reduction

proof.text: For any reduced modification $h:X\to C$ and a fibre-generic $c\in C_t$, every point $x\in h^{-1}(c)$ is fibre-generic in $X_t$. Indeed [lem-sc-closed-irreducible-dimension-trdeg] identifies the residue transcendence degrees over $\kappa(t)$ of $c$ and of a fibre-generic point with $1$; all points of a pure one-dimensional finite-type fibre have transcendence degree at most $1$, since their closures lie in a one-dimensional component. The embedding $\kappa(c)\hookrightarrow\kappa(x)$ and [lem-kun-transcendence-degree-tower] force the latter degree to be $1$. The closure of $x$ therefore has dimension $1$ and must be a whole component. Hence $h^{-1}(c)$ is finite. By [lem-trf-proper-finite-fibre-finite-near], $h$ is finite over a neighbourhood of $c$; shrink to an affine open of the integral normal $C$. The restriction remains integral and birational, so [lem-trf-finite-birational-normal-iso] makes it an isomorphism.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.1: finite fibres over fibre-generic points and finite birational normal isomorphism

proof.text: Let $Z\subseteq C$ be the reduced closed complement of the largest isomorphism open of $q$. Step 2 shows that $Z_t$ contains no generic point of any component of $C_t$. Since $C_t$ is a Noetherian pure curve, a proper closed subset of each of its finitely many one-dimensional components has dimension at most zero (a positive chain could otherwise be extended by that component to a chain of length at least two). Thus every nonempty $Z_t$ has dimension zero. The closed subscheme $Z$ is of finite type over $T$, because its affine rings are quotients of those of $C$. Now [lem-trf-locally-quasi-finite-relative-dimension-zero] makes $Z\to T$ locally quasi-finite; finite type and the zero-dimensional finite-type fibres give quasi-finiteness in [pqf-def-quasifinite].

source.place: Lemma 4.2.1(ii), modification locus avoids fibre-generic points

proof.text: Let $X$ now be any normal curve occurring as a modification, and let $x\in X$ be fibre-generic. A valuation ring $O$ of its component function field $L$ dominating $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ exists by [lemma-nagata-local-domain-valuation-dominates], and gives a centred valuation. Step 2, with $X$ as normal target, says that every integral proper birational model $X^{\prime}\to X$ is an isomorphism near $x$. Its centre $x^{\prime}$ therefore has local ring exactly $\mathcal O_{X,x}\subseteq L$. Apply [lem-trf-birational-riemann-zariski-neighbourhoods](iii): every $a\in O$ belongs to an affine neighbourhood ring of such a centre, hence belongs to $\mathcal O_{X^{\prime},x^{\prime}}=\mathcal O_{X,x}$. The reverse inclusion is domination. Thus $O=\mathcal O_{X,x}$, and this proves both existence and uniqueness of a centred valuation above every fibre-generic point of a normal modification.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.1 and the paragraph following it: fibre-generic local rings are valuation rings

proof.text: For this unique valuation ring $O=\mathcal O_{X,x}$, put $t=f(x)$ and $\mathfrak p\subset V$ its corresponding prime. The local structural map $V_{\mathfrak p}\to\mathcal O_{X,x}$ has maximal-ideal contraction $\mathfrak pV_{\mathfrak p}$. In fact $O\cap K=V_{\mathfrak p}$: if $a\in K\setminus V_{\mathfrak p}$, the valuation property of $V_{\mathfrak p}$ gives $a^{-1}\in\mathfrak pV_{\mathfrak p}$, so $a^{-1}$ is a nonunit of $O$ and $a\notin O$. Consequently $\kappa(O\cap K)=\kappa(t)$ and $\kappa(O)=\kappa(x)$. By [lem-sc-closed-irreducible-dimension-trdeg] the latter has transcendence degree one over $\kappa(t)$. This proves the residue assertion for every normal modification, including $C$.

source.place: Section 4.2, definition of the residual-transcendence-degree-one subset

proof.text: Normalize the integral $Y$ by [lem-trf-valuation-curve-finite-normalization], obtaining a finite surjective $n:M\to Y$ with $M$ a normal $T$-curve and with the same generic fibre. The composite $M\to C$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper] and [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence], and is a modification. The proper lifts of each centred valuation through $Y$ and $M$ agree by uniqueness in [lem-trf-birational-riemann-zariski-neighbourhoods]. A point $m$ and its image $y$ have a finite residue-field extension: on a fibre of a finite map the coordinate algebra is finite-dimensional over $\kappa(y)$, and its residue fields are finite-dimensional quotients. Thus [lem-kun-transcendence-degree-tower] and [lem-sc-closed-irreducible-dimension-trdeg] show that $m$ is fibre-generic exactly when $y$ is. Hence $\Gamma(M)=\Gamma(Y)$ and $\Gamma_0(M)=\Gamma_0(Y)$. Steps 4--5 for $M$ give the residual transcendence degree assertion for $Y$. For every fibre-generic $y\in Y$, choose a point of its nonempty finite inverse image in $M$ and use step 4; this also proves the asserted surjectivity of centres for reduced $Y$.

source.place: Section 4.1 normalization; reduced-source extension of Lemma 4.2.2

proof.text: There are finitely many $t\in T$, and each $M_t$ has finitely many components by step 1. Step 4 bijects their generic points with $\Gamma(M)$. It follows that $\Gamma(M)$, and therefore its subset $\Gamma_0(M)=\Gamma_0(Y)$, is finite. By [lem-trf-flat-fibre-generic-generalization] the fibre-generic locus of $M$ is stable under generalization. Its inverse image under the continuous centre map is $\Gamma(M)=\Gamma(Y)$, so this set is also stable under generalization. Step 2 gives $\Gamma(C)\subseteq\Gamma(Y)$, since every valuation with fibre-generic centre on $C$ lifts through an isomorphism neighbourhood. Therefore $\operatorname{gen}(\Gamma_0(Y))\cup\Gamma(C)\subseteq\Gamma(Y)$.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.2, finiteness and the easy inclusion

proof.text: For the converse let $\nu\in\Gamma(Y)\setminus\Gamma(C)$, with centre $x\in M_t$, and put $c=q n(x)$. Then $c$ is closed in $C_t$: otherwise it would be a generic point of the pure curve, by [lem-kun-closed-point-field] and [lem-sc-closed-irreducible-dimension-trdeg]. Let $H=\overline{\{x\}}\subseteq M$ and $B=\overline{\{c\}}\subseteq C$, with reduced closed-subscheme structures. The closed map $qn$ gives $(qn)(H)=B$: continuity gives containment in $B$, and closedness gives the reverse containment. By [lem-trf-flat-fibre-component-closure-dimension], every nonempty fibre of $H$ is pure of dimension one.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.2, converse inclusion: closures of a contracted fibre component

proof.text: Every nonempty fibre of $B$ has dimension zero. To check this at $s$ in its image, use an affine open $W\subseteq C$ meeting $B_s$. It contains $c$, since $c$ is the generic point of $B$. If $\mathfrak p\subset V$ is the prime of $t$, the domain $D=\Gamma(B\cap W,\mathcal O_B)$ is a finite-type algebra containing $V/\mathfrak p$, and its generic fibre over this valuation domain is the single point $c$ with field $\kappa(c)$, finite over $\kappa(t)$ by [lem-kun-closed-point-field]. Localize $V/\mathfrak p$ at the prime of $s$. Apply [lem-trf-valuation-domain-fibre-dimensions] to the resulting finite-type domain: its generic fibre has dimension zero, so its nonempty closed fibre does too. These affine opens cover $B_s$. This applies the existing dimension theorem to a quotient and a localization of the valuation ring; no Noetherian assumption on $V$ is used.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.2, the image has zero-dimensional base fibres; Stacks Tag 00QK supplies the point-closure calculation

proof.text: Choose the most specialized point $s$ in the nonempty image of $H\to T$; it exists because $T$ is a finite chain. Its inverse image $H_s$ is closed in $H$: the inverse image of $\overline{\{s\}}$ equals $H_s$ because no stricter specialization occurs in that image. Pick a component $D$ of $H_s$ with generic point $y$. Step 8 gives $\dim D=1$. Since $D$ is a closed irreducible subset of the pure curve $M_s$, it is also a component of $M_s$. Step 9 says that the image of this irreducible $D$ in $B_s$ is a single point, as a zero-dimensional Noetherian space has only singleton irreducible subsets. Moreover $D$ is closed in $M$, and $qn$ is closed, so this image point is closed in all of $C$. Step 4 now gives a valuation $\mu=\mathcal O_{M,y}$ in $\Gamma_0(Y)$.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.2, choose a last nonempty fibre of the component closure

proof.text:
The point $x$ generalizes $y$ in $M$, and the two corresponding valuation rings satisfy $\mathcal O_{M,y}\subseteq\mathcal O_{M,x}$; the latter is the localization of the former at the prime corresponding to $x$. The map $\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{M,y}	o M$ therefore restricts on this localization to the centred map for $
u$. Lift it to any proper birational model over $C$ using [lem-trf-birational-riemann-zariski-neighbourhoods]. Its restriction is the unique lift of $
u$, while its closed point is the centre of $\mu$. Continuity makes the former centre a generalization of the latter on every model. Since inverse images of opens under these centre maps generate the topology, every neighbourhood of $\mu$ contains $
u$. Thus $
u\in\operatorname{gen}(\Gamma_0(Y))$. Together with step 7 this proves the stated equality. The finite disjoint component reduction of step 1 preserves every set and specialization relation used above, completing all clauses.
